findings.issue: General and special taxes FY2026-27 not yet due; FY2025-26 both installments PAID; no Mello-Roos of record.
findings.rationale: No open tax lien. Standard exception.

findings.issue: Unreleased deed of trust ($485,000; dated 09/22/2009; recorded 10/03/2009). Beneficiary Pacific Rim Savings Bank, FSB closed by FDIC 03/04/2011. Successor in interest NOT reflected in chain of title. No reconveyance of record. Full reconveyance, substitution of trustee, or payoff demand from FDIC as receiver required before title is insurable.
findings.rationale: Not a standard Schedule B exception — this is an active monetary encumbrance that prevents insurable title. Even with Torres's flexible approach to Schedule B, there is no identified party from whom a routine payoff or reconveyance can be obtained. The FDIC receivership gap creates genuine title risk. Bayline deal-breaker: monetary liens cannot carry into title.
findings.precedent: Folsom-St-2026-SL Exc. 3 (Sarah Lin same document, same finding — RED). Mission-St-2025-SL: FDIC payoff demand + 110% escrow holdback + recorded reconveyance applied.

findings.issue: Active SFPUC sewer easement (8-ft wide; recorded 06/07/1971). Survey SFM-2026-0341 (LS Brunetti, 07/09/2026) locates easement centerline beneath NE building foundation corner; ~2.3 ft encroachment into building envelope at foundation corner. 36-inch combined sewer main confirmed active by SFPUC. No encroachment permit of record. ALTA extended coverage blocked by title company pending SFPUC encroachment agreement and senior underwriting endorsement.
findings.rationale: Easement is located on survey — Torres's threshold is met. Torres does not require ALTA extended coverage, so the title company's ALTA blockage is not independently a RED finding for Torres. Bayline explicitly accepts active sewer/utility easement risk without requiring cure. The ~2.3 ft physical encroachment into the building foundation warrants disclosure, an SFPUC encroachment assessment, and a structural engineer's opinion on foundation integrity — but is acceptable at AMBER given Bayline's risk tolerance. KEY DIVERGENCE: Sarah Lin flagged this RED due to ALTA blockage — that rule does not apply to Torres.
findings.precedent: Folsom-St-2026-SL Exc. 4 (Sarah Lin: RED due to ALTA blockage — ALTA requirement does not apply to Torres/Bayline).

findings.issue: CC&Rs (recorded 08/14/1947, amended 11/02/1988). §4.2 rental cap: max 1 unit rentable; one unit must be owner-occupied; LLC buyer cannot owner-occupy; $500/mo LD per violation enforceable by Block 4027 Lots 16-22 owners. §4.5 alteration restriction: majority neighbor consent required for structural alterations. Runs to 08/14/2047.
findings.rationale: Bayline accepts CC&R risk including rental caps and use restrictions, subject to counsel review. §4.2 directly conflicts with LLC buyer structure — no natural person available to satisfy owner-occupancy requirement; full rental income from both units potentially at risk. §4.5 may impede redevelopment work. Counsel opinion on enforceability under Civil Code §714.7 required before COE.

findings.issue: Active mechanics' lien: Bay Area Masonry & Structural Repair Inc. v. Dmitri A. Volkov; $38,750; foundation work; recorded 05/29/2026 (Series 2026-F118843). 90-day enforcement window (CCP §8460) expires approx. 08/27/2026. No action on file as of report date. Release or 1.5x bond ($58,125) required.
findings.rationale: Bayline deal-breaker: uncleared monetary liens cannot carry into title. Seller has committed in PA §5.D.6 to provide release, bond, or $58,125 purchase price credit — that commitment is noted but not yet performed. The enforcement window (~08/27/2026) closes two days before the scheduled COE (08/29/2026), creating timing urgency.

findings.issue: SF Rent Ordinance (Admin. Code Ch. 37) informational notice. Not an exception to title. Note: property records disclose Unit 2 tenant Raymond T. Castellanos, move-in March 2003 (23+ years), confirmed rent-ordinance-protected.
findings.rationale: Torres's protective clause is triggered by this disclosure: a protected tenancy with 23+ years of occupancy has been identified. No estoppel certificate is referenced in the title report. This finding establishes the factual basis for a full RED treatment in the purchase agreement review. Bayline deal-breaker: protected tenancy without documented vacancy plan.

findings.issue: Rights of parties in possession not shown by public records; two residential tenancies disclosed by seller; terms off-record.
findings.rationale: Standard Schedule B exception under CLTA. Torres accepts standard exceptions AMBER with disclosure. Cross-references Exc. 7: Unit 2 (Castellanos) is a confirmed rent-ordinance-protected tenancy. Estoppel certificate and vacancy plan required in PA review before this risk is acceptable to Torres.

findings.issue: Seismic Hazard Zone — Liquefaction designation (PRC §§2690-2699.6). Mandatory NHD disclosure (Civ. Code §1103). 1924 construction.
findings.rationale: Mandatory statutory disclosure. A 1924 structure in a liquefaction zone carries inherent seismic risk. The active sewer main encroachment at the building foundation (Exc. 4) compounds the structural exposure. Seismic/structural engineering assessment recommended before COE.

findings.issue: 1924 construction; no Certificate of Final Completion for any post-1980 work per SF Planning Dept records. DBI permit history not yet reviewed.
findings.rationale: Pre-1980 structure. DBI permit history pull required — particularly in light of the unpermitted rear addition disclosed in the PA (approx. 110 sq ft + 180 sq ft deck, constructed ~2018 with no permit). This finding establishes the factual predicate for Torres's 17-day inspection contingency hard floor: the property is pre-1980 and the inspection scope is substantial. The 10-day inspection contingency in PA §14.B will be flagged RED.
